_about: What the game says about the novel (flavor.json novelNotes: the 'In the Novel' line on each ending screen and in the Ledger), claim by claim. 'fact' claims carry a short passage from the 1818 text that is checked to be in the chapter named (npm run check:claims). 'reading' claims are interpretation, with the passage that prompts it. 'absence' claims say something is not in the book; a passage cannot show that, so they were checked by reading, and are listed for a reader who knows the book to confirm.
source: claims/source/frankenstein-1818.txt (Project Gutenberg #41445, the 1818 first edition, three volumes)

claims.claim: The creature, at the very end, speaks of collecting his funeral pile in the far north and ascending it.
claims.evidence: I shall ascend my funeral pile triumphantly

claims.claim: Victor does not burn his laboratory down.
claims.how: read through; the only destruction of apparatus is the female creature's (Vol. III, ch. 3), by tearing, not fire

claims.claim: The creature says he is alone, in contrast to the devil of Paradise Lost who had companions.
claims.evidence: I am quite alone

claims.claim: There is no army of grafted creatures; there is one creature.
claims.how: read through; Victor makes one creature and destroys the second before it is animated

claims.claim: Victor pursues the creature, reserved for vengeance.
claims.evidence: I was reserved for vengeance

claims.claim: Victor dies aboard Walton's ship.
claims.evidence: his eyes closed for ever

claims.claim: Walton's crew sees a traveller on the Arctic ice, and later takes Victor aboard.
claims.evidence: lost among the distant inequalities of the ice

claims.claim: Victor takes the female creature to one of the remotest of the Orkneys.
claims.evidence: fixed on one of the remotest of the Orkneys

claims.claim: He destroys it before it is animated, with the creature watching.
claims.evidence: tore to pieces the thing on which I was engaged

claims.claim: The creature promises to be with him on his wedding-night.
claims.evidence: I shall be with you on your wedding-night

claims.claim: Victor is told a gentleman was found murdered the night before (it is Clerval).
claims.evidence: a gentleman who was found murdered here last night

claims.claim: Elizabeth is killed on her wedding night (Victor hears her scream and the truth rushes in).
claims.evidence: the whole truth rushed into my mind

claims.claim: The novel's subtitle is The Modern Prometheus.
claims.evidence: FRANKENSTEIN; OR, THE MODERN PROMETHEUS

claims.claim: Its Prometheus is Victor, who takes the power of making life and is ruined by what he has made.
claims.evidence: I was reserved for vengeance

claims.claim: The creature learns the ideas that belong to words, and to say them, by overhearing the cottagers.
claims.evidence: I cannot describe the delight I felt when I learned the ideas appropriated to each of these sounds

claims.claim: He watches the family from a hovel through a chink in its wall.
claims.evidence: looking through a small chink

claims.claim: Victor runs from the creature the night it wakes.
claims.evidence: I rushed out of the room

claims.claim: He sees it again by a flash of lightning the night William is killed.
claims.evidence: A flash of lightning illuminated the object

claims.claim: On the glacier the creature asks Victor to hear him.
claims.evidence: Be calm! I entreat you to hear me

claims.claim: Victor first refuses.
claims.evidence: Begone! I will not hear you

claims.claim: Then he consents to listen.
claims.evidence: But I consented to listen

claims.claim: Justine is condemned for William's murder.
claims.evidence: Justine was condemned

claims.claim: Victor does not say what he knows, because it would be taken for madness.
claims.evidence: the ravings of a madman

claims.claim: The story survives because Walton records Victor's account as nearly as possible in his own words.
claims.evidence: to record, as nearly as possible in his own words, what he has related during the day

claims.claim: Victor takes no professorship and publishes nothing.
claims.how: read through; he returns to Geneva, then travels, and never takes a post or publishes

claims.claim: At Justine's trial the truth is known to Victor, who stays silent.
claims.evidence: the ravings of a madman

claims.claim: The blind De Lacey is one of the few the creature pleads with.
claims.evidence: I am an unfortunate and deserted creature

claims.claim: Victor on the glacier is another.
claims.evidence: Be calm! I entreat you to hear me

claims.claim: Walton, over Victor's body, is the last.
claims.evidence: I am quite alone

claims.claim: The creature never speaks before a crowd.
claims.how: read through; the villagers and the cottagers meet him with blows and he does not speak

claims.claim: The work succeeds, and Victor is overcome with horror at once.
claims.evidence: breathless horror and disgust

claims.claim: Victor's materials come from the dissecting room and the slaughter-house.
claims.evidence: The dissecting room and the slaughter-house furnished many of my materials

claims.claim: The creature's hunger comes later, in the forest.
claims.evidence: I felt tormented by hunger and thirst

claims.claim: Victor tells the whole story to a Geneva magistrate, who half believes it and will not act.
claims.evidence: the whole tide of his incredulity returned
